summary: Autonomous driving is the visible front, but AI runs through freight matching, maritime navigation, transit operations, and aviation. Who tracks it: the safety regulators and standards bodies are the primary record, with the operators' own published data layered on top.

analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau, 13.0% of firms in transportation and warehousing (NAICS 48-49) answered yes to whether they had used AI in the last two weeks, up from 7.9% in the prior period, with the question first asked in September 2023. That is the only measured adoption figure in this material, and it covers the sector as a whole rather than any single mode.

The sources show AI arriving through operations rather than through one flagship product. Samsara describes a connected operations platform used by 20,000+ operations, with AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching and drowsiness detection, and credits those safety technologies with 380,000+ accidents prevented. C.H. Robinson frames its managed solutions as autonomous logistics orchestration, where the supply chain analyzes, decides, executes and improves across every shipment, and runs an AI assistant on its site to help with shipping options. Aurora describes self-driving freight powered by the Aurora Driver, built with hardware and software backed by verifiable AI and integrated into fleets.

The vendor layer here is concentrated among a small number of named players. Aurora and Kodiak are described as pure-play autonomous trucking platforms operating Level 4 freight on commercial highway corridors. Waymo publishes a safety hub with methodology and crash-rate comparisons, which this site calls the most complete public evidence base from an AV operator. Airbus says it works with its innovation ecosystem on a decarbonised, connected and autonomous future for aerospace, and this site pairs Airbus's innovation programs with Boeing's autonomy work on AI flight management and predictive maintenance. Wärtsilä supplies AI-driven predictive analytics to marine and energy customers. Samsara and Mobileye sit in fleet telematics and computer vision, and Palantir is tracked on this site as the enterprise AI platform used by airlines and rail operators for fleet and crew optimization. The American Trucking Associations describes itself as the largest national trade association for trucking, with more than 37,000 members, and this site tracks it as the industry body following policy and adoption for autonomous freight and AI logistics.

Hard return figures are thin. The clearest numbers come from Samsara's 380,000+ accidents prevented and from a partner quoted on Aurora's site, who calls early pilot results impressive, particularly autonomous hauling between Fort Worth and El Paso, and describes a hybrid model of professional drivers and the Aurora Driver. The same page carries a projection that freight volumes will grow five fold between 2010-2050, which the partner uses to argue autonomous transport is a necessity rather than an innovation. Beyond that, the sources assert safety and efficiency benefits without publishing measured returns.

Regulation is being written now, and it is mode by mode. The IMO adopted a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships in May 2026, effective 1 July 2026, a goal-based framework that is voluntary guidance, technology-neutral, and designed to facilitate a future transition into a mandatory instrument. The IMO states that at present there are no commercially operating, internationally trading SOLAS cargo ships that operate autonomously or remotely controlled, though trials have shown that larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible. EASA's Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 sets out its vision for the safety and ethical considerations of AI in aviation, with a comprehensive action plan and annual amendment. Waymo frames its safety program around Vision Zero and the U.S. Department of Transportation National Roadway Safety Strategy, and this site notes that the FAA's innovation work and EASA's roadmap are the regulatory record for AI flight systems, automated risk management and eVTOL certification.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the material points to the operational entry points with the most evidence, telematics, driver monitoring, predictive maintenance and freight matching, where Samsara and C.H. Robinson describe systems already in use, rather than full autonomy, which the IMO places mostly in trials for commercial international shipping and which Aurora describes through pilots and partnerships. The compliance question depends on mode, since maritime now holds a code and aviation holds agency roadmaps. The World of AI's own robotics model catalogue tracks the 1000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, refreshed daily, which is a view of the underlying model supply rather than a deployment record.

https://www.samsara.com/.brief: Samsara claims its connected operations platform supports more than 20,000 operations in improving safety, cutting costs, and running smarter. The platform analyzes data to provide AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, and actionable insights that help spot risks and optimize operations. According to Samsara, its AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching, and other safety technologies have prevented over 380,000 accidents. The system includes cameras and video AI, multicam support, driver experience tools, driver coaching, drowsiness detection, safety reporting & insights, and equipment management.

https://www.trucking.org/.brief: ATA, the American Trucking Association, says it is the largest and most comprehensive national trade association for trucking. It reports that Miguel Corral, a UPS driver, was named Bendix Grand Champion at the 2026 National Truck Driving & Step Van Championships. ATA says it has more than 37,000 members, including carriers, suppliers, shippers, and professionals, and that it works to influence government policy, educate stakeholders, and host events that bring together all parts of the industry.

https://www.wartsila.com/.brief: Wärtsilä claims it is a global leader in innovative technologies and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy markets. The company says it already has most of the technology needed to decarbonise, from engines that can run flexibly on low- and zero-carbon fuels to AI-driven predictive analytics. Wärtsilä is using these tools to help customers take the next step on their decarbonisation journey.

https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/re.brief: The EASA has published an Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 that outlines the Agency's approach to safety and ethical considerations for AI in aviation. The roadmap provides an action plan for the EASA AI Programme, including conceptual guidance and anticipated rulemaking activities, and serves as a basis for stakeholder discussions. As a living document, it will be updated annually and refined through stakeholder exchanges and the Agency's ongoing practical work on AI development.

https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/HotTo.brief: The IMO introduced a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) in May 2026, which became effective on 1 July 2026. A ship is considered a MASS only when autonomous or remote technologies replace or support crew functions and it holds a valid MASS Safety Certificate; enhanced automation alone does not qualify. The Code offers voluntary, technology-neutral guidance that complements existing regulations and defines operating conditions, limits, and responses when those limits are exceeded, creating a “goal-based framework” for safe design, operation, and certification. Trials under interim MSC 110 guidelines in June 2019 have shown that larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible, and while no SOLAS cargo ships are yet operating autonomously, the IMO anticipates commercial service in the near future with a gradual evolution toward more advanced MASS. An IMO seminar in April 2024 addressed the implications, challenges, and opportunities of MASS for ports and public authorities.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: The World of AI presents a catalogue of the 1,000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub. For each entry, the page lists its licence, download count, and release date, and the catalogue is refreshed daily using the Hub’s public API, sorted by all-time downloads. The page states that every model links to its own Hugging Face page. It also records that the information was last verified on 2026-09-25.
